stories.title: Breaking the barrier: exercise preferences and motivational factors in stressed Chinese secondary school students
stories.description: This study explores the motivations, barriers, and exercise preferences among Chinese secondary school students experiencing psychological stress. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 29 adolescent students, and a deductive analysis was employed to identify key themes related to their exercise behaviors. To ensure objectivity and minimize bias, data were triangulated. The findings revealed seven motivational themes driving exercise participation, health benefits, external encouragement and supervision, body shaping, personal inspiration, academic performance, enjoyment, and prior exercise experiences. Conversely, five key barriers were identified: academic pressure, negative exercise experiences, lack of motivation, illness, and adverse weather conditions. Participants generally preferred moderate to vigorous group-based exercises lasting 30 to 60 min, 3–5 times per week. Gender differences emerged in both barriers and motivations: girls were more likely to forgo exercise due to academic demands, while boys cited illness as a primary obstacle. Additionally, girls reported needing more external encouragement to engage in exercise, whereas boys required greater personal inspiration. These insights can inform the design of targeted exercise programs to effectively reduce stress in this population.
